accepted_path.meaning: starts a bounded trial from committed authority and immutable checkpoint
clones committed physical state and calls the canonical interval runtime without mutating external committed state
owns private working state, transaction retries/substeps and whole-request completion; only a completed canonical interval moves working state to its candidate authority
executes full/half trials, evaluates solver/mass/temporal acceptance, retries from checkpoint and publishes only accepted transaction state
delegates candidate commit to kernel commit semantics
atomically replaces committed physical state, increments revision and advances committed time only after provenance/time validation

observation_surface.interval_result: kernel_result_t / canonical_result_t-derived accepted mass and diagnostics
observation_surface.rule: Research observations are taken after successful FMR commit. Candidate/rejected state observations, if retained for numerical diagnostics, are tagged separately and never enter the accepted trajectory library.

key_semantic_findings: run_canonical_interval keeps the externally committed state untouched until the full requested interval completes.
execute_reference_interval retries from a checkpoint when solver, mass or temporal acceptance fails.
kernel commit is the external committed-state mutation boundary.
The superseded direct-solver pilot sat below these acceptance/commit layers and therefore cannot define ROM reference trajectories.
